## ADR-582 - KerfDesk Remote: one app for the phone and MCP hosts

**Status:** Accepted for the maintainer's request on 10 October 2026 to rebuild Phone & MCP as a real app ("build all for main design and then also all that needs extra approval"). Extends ADR-564, ADR-568 and ADR-569. Source, hosted Worker, installed desktop, live MCP host, physical phone and hardware evidence remain separate.

**Context.** The phone page was ~3,800 lines of hand-written DOM code. The MCP Apps panel was HTML inside TypeScript strings, partly generated by stripping imports with a regular expression. The two drifted. The canvas was a bounded PNG with bounding-box selection, "live" meant five-second polling through the full relay round trip, the page could not be installed, and the MCP panel used none of the host's display-mode, sizing, model-context or app-tool capabilities.

**Decision.**

1. **One codebase.** `services/remote-control/app/` holds `src/core/` (state, transports, scene geometry, controller) and `src/ui/` (React components and the design system), with `src/mcp/` for host integration. `scripts/build-app.mjs` builds two targets: an installable web app served by the existing Worker at `/app/` (fixed asset allowlist, its own CSP with `manifest-src`/`worker-src 'self'`, camera allowed for QR pairing), and a self-contained HTML document in `electron/mcp/workspace-app-ui.ts` registered as `ui://kerfdesk/workspace/v6.html` (`text/html;profile=mcp-app`, empty CSP allowlists). Generated output is committed and `--check`ed in `build`, `format:check` and `deploy`, like the touch and scanner assets. New desktop pairing links open `/app/`; the old `/control` page stays for printed links until the new app reaches parity in production use. The v5 panel source stays only for its regression tests.
2. **Transport abstraction.** The phone transport uses the existing cookie session, CSRF header and `/api/client/command`. The MCP transport calls tools through the host's authenticated connection using `@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps` (MIT, 2.0.3, peers on the same SDK v2 major). The UI never selects a URL or holds a credential.
3. **Live changes.** The desktop renderer reports a monotonic change counter and a machine-status sequence through its existing private routes. Electron main forwards `{v:1,type:'changed',revision,machineSeq}` to its Durable Object only when a value changes. The message carries no artwork. The Durable Object fans this out to approved phone WebSockets (`GET /api/client/socket`, same cookie, exact Origin, live session/lease/scope checks on upgrade and on every frame) and resolves the new read command `wait_for_change` without contacting the desktop. Clients then read the changed projection. Older desktops never send `changed`; clients fall back to bounded polling.
4. **Vector scene.** New read command `get_workspace_scene` returns a bounded, revisioned projection of visible artwork in scene millimetres. It includes stable IDs, kind, transform-applied flattened polylines (closed flag), layer colour, operation assignment, group, locked/editable flags and bounds, plus the bed. It requires the existing default-off artwork-sharing opt-in because geometry reveals artwork. Raster images contribute their transformed placement footprint only, as in ADR-568 Amendment 1. Points are encoded as hundredths of a millimetre with tolerance-bounded simplification. Hard caps on objects, points and bytes return an explicit `unavailable` status with a reason; geometry is never silently dropped. Without the opt-in, the canvas shows artwork bounds from `get_workspace`. The PNG preview stays for non-UI MCP clients and older desktops.
5. **Fluid editing.** Move, resize and rotate commit on gesture end as one existing revision-fenced, idempotent mutation with shared Undo. Drawing keeps an explicit Apply. The client renders optimistically and snaps back on `stale_revision` while keeping the user's draft.
6. **MCP host integration.** The panel opens inline as a compact card (two primary actions), requests fullscreen for editing, and uses picture-in-picture only when the host lists it. It sends size changes, publishes a bounded `updateModelContext` summary of the visible view and selection, and registers view-only app tools (`ui_show`, `ui_focus`, `ui_highlight`, `ui_get_view_state`). These app tools change only the panel; they have no PC side effects and grant no authority. Content returned to the model is labelled as user data.
7. **Design language.** The app reuses the desktop tokens (warm neutrals, copper accent, blue canvas selection, danger red), defaults to light with a dark theme, follows the MCP host theme, and keeps 48 px touch targets, numeric alternatives to every gesture and visible reasons for unavailable actions. A persistent Abort dock reserves its own layout space for control-approved connections whenever motion or a job is active.

**Unchanged.** PC approval, scopes, revision fences, request identities, the action ledger, the Abort lane, frame-first Start (ADR-565), the Pro admission rule (ADR-540), artwork-sharing opt-in, and every exclusion in ADR-564/569 that later ADRs do not explicitly amend. Navigation, refresh, model context and app tools grant no authority.

**Consequences.** The desktop and relay must both be updated before `changed`, `wait_for_change`, sockets and scenes work; the app detects their absence and degrades. Bundled React and ext-apps must appear in the service notices. Hosted deployment, a real MCP host and a physical phone are separate qualification lanes.
